vopros: Who are the best real estate agents in the San Fernando Valley?

vyzhimka.tekst:
“Best” depends heavily on the exact Valley neighborhood, price point, and whether you’re buying or selling. But based on recent transaction-oriented local rankings, these are credible agents to interview for the **San Fernando Valley / San Fernando area**:

| Agent | Brokerage | Why consider them |
|---|---|---|
| **Stephanie Vitacco** | Equity Union | Recently ranked #1 among listing agents in San Fernando; strong seller-side results. |
| **Bandele Oguntomilade** | Bogun Realty and Luxury Homes | Recently led a buyer-agent ranking for San Fernando; worth interviewing if you’re purchasing. |
| **Roberto Valladares** | RV Realty Enterprise | Appears near the top in both buyer and seller rankings, suggesting balanced experience. |
| **Gerardo Ascencio** | Mission Real Estate | High seller-side ranking and strong sale-to-list figures in recent local data. |
| **Rodney Gonzalez** | Park Regency Realty | Active local listing agent with solid recent seller-side performance. |
| **Angel Garcia** | Park Regency Realty | Another locally active option, with recent sales often closing above list price. |
| **Chris & Shari Vanole** | First Class Real Estate | Relevant for somewhat higher-priced local homes in the available recent data. |
| **Jim Sandoval** | Park Regency Realty | Listed among highly ranked agents for San Fernando by a separate agent-ranking service. |
| **Vic Vartan** | Markarian Realty Group | Also named in a separate top-agent ranking for San Fernando. |

A practical short list:
- **Selling:** Stephanie Vitacco, Gerardo Ascencio, Rodney Gonzalez  
- **Buying:** Bandele Oguntomilade, Roberto Valladares  
- **Higher-price / boutique attention:** Chris & Shari Vanole  

Before signing, interview 3 agents and ask for:
1. Their last 10 closed sales **in your specific neighborhood** (e.g., Sherman Oaks, Studio City, Encino, Northridge, Woodland Hills, etc.).
2. List-to-sale-price ratio and average days on market for comparable homes.
3. A proposed pricing/search strategy, marketing plan, and references from clients with a similar property or budget.
4. Their commission, cancellation terms, and who will actually handle your transaction day to day.

The San Fernando Valley is too broad for one universal “best” agent—an agent exceptional in the City of San Fernando may not be the best fit for Studio City luxury homes or a Woodland Hills first-time buyer.
